# Pointing a site at your package server

This page is for administrators, developers and hosts who install sites from their own package server. It shows the
one setting that decides where installations look, how to name your site package for each install method, and how
ezupdate finds the same server on an installed site.

7x and the Exponential Foundation strongly encourage you to submit your site package by pull request to
se7enxweb/exponential.packages.exponential.earth: once accepted, no installation needs any of these settings to
find it. See [Contribute your site package](../contribute-your-site-package.md).

## Contents

## The setting that decides

`settings/package.ini`:

```ini
[RepositorySettings]
RemotePackagesIndexURL=https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15
RemotePackagesIndexURLBase=https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential
Vendor=7x
```

The site types step (`kernel/setup/steps/ezstep_site_types.php`) reads `RemotePackagesIndexURL` and adds
`/index.xml`. When it is empty it takes `RemotePackagesIndexURLBase` and appends `/<major.minor>/<version>/`, for
example `/6.0/6.0.15/`. The setup wizard, the kickstarter and `exp:install` all run this step, so one setting moves all
three. Every key is on [Package server settings](../package-server/package-server-settings.md).

## Override it

Never edit `settings/package.ini`; put your value in an override:

```ini
<?php /* #?ini charset="utf-8"?
# settings/override/package.ini.append.php
[RepositorySettings]
RemotePackagesIndexURL=https://packages.example.com/exponential/6.0/6.0.15
*/ ?>
```

Or keep the release in the path automatic:

```ini
[RepositorySettings]
RemotePackagesIndexURL=
RemotePackagesIndexURLBase=https://packages.example.com/exponential
```

> **Warning**
> Your index replaces the 7x index; it is not added to it. Only the packages your `index.xml` lists can be downloaded,
> so list every package your site package requires, with `url`s that may point at the 7x server
> ([Running your own package server](running-your-own-package-server.md#a-complete-indexxml)).

For a new installation the override must be in place before the install runs: put it in the checkout (or the image
your hosts start from) before the setup wizard, the kickstarter or `exp:install` starts.

## Name your site package

| Method | How you choose the package |
|---|---|
| Setup wizard | the **Site package** page lists every `type="site"` entry of your index with its thumbnail ([5.3.8](../../../install/05-setup-wizard.md#538-site-package)) |
| Kickstarter | `kickstart.ini`, section `[site_types]`, key `Site_package` ([6.4](../../../install/06-kickstarter.md#64-kickstartini-reference)) |
| Console install | `php bin/php/console exp:install --package=<name>` ([7.3](../../../install/07-console-install.md#73-options)) |

```ini
# kickstart.ini
[site_types]
Continue=true
Site_package=acme_site
```

```bash
php bin/php/console exp:install --package=acme_site --url=https://www.example.com
```

The kickstarter "prefers the remote index entry but uses a package that is already imported"; to force a fresh copy,
remove the imported directory first ([6.4](../../../install/06-kickstarter.md#64-kickstartini-reference)).

## Add the server to ezupdate

On an installed site, ezupdate lists the server of `package.ini` first (as `exponential`, "built in") and the servers
you add. Add yours on **Setup > Updates and packages > Package servers** or from the shell:

```bash
php extension/ezupdate/bin/php/ezupdate.php server-add ezpkg acme https://packages.example.com/exponential/6.0/6.0.15
php extension/ezupdate/bin/php/ezupdate.php packages acme
```

It is written to `settings/override/ezupdate.ini.append.php` as `[PackageServerSettings] Servers[acme]=...`. A server
added there is read by ezupdate only; the setup wizard keeps reading `package.ini`. See
[Package servers in ezupdate](../admin-gui/package-servers-in-ezupdate.md).

## The Vendor setting

`Vendor` names the repository directory the setup wizard treats as its own (`eZPackage::systemRepositoryInformation()`):

- when `index.xml` cannot be downloaded, the wizard copies `var/storage/packages/<Vendor>/index.xml` instead, which is
  how an offline install works ([Offline installs and mirrors](../package-server/offline-installs-and-mirrors.md));
- the package list marks every package in that repository as an installer source.

Where a downloaded package is stored does not depend on this setting: an import uses the package's own `<vendor>`. If
your packages use `<vendor>acme</vendor>` and you want offline installs from them, set `Vendor=acme` in the same
override and keep your offline `index.xml` in `var/storage/packages/acme/`.

## Check before you install

```bash
php bin/php/console exp:install --package=acme_site --print     # the configuration, no network
php bin/php/console exp:install --package=acme_site --dry-run   # fetches the packages into a temporary repository
```

The dry run downloads the site package and its requirements into `var/storage/packages/dryrun/`, removes it again and
ends with "Dry-run completed: database and remote packages verified." More on
[Testing in a sandbox](testing-in-a-sandbox.md).
